companyAlerts.tradingDesc: Inventory and COGS must be configured for merchandise inventory recording. Withholding tax is optional.

descriptions.vatInput: PPN Masukan (Asset account) tracks VAT paid on purchases that can be credited when remitting tax.
descriptions.vatOutput: PPN Keluaran (Liability account) tracks VAT collected from customers to be remitted to the government.
descriptions.taxRemittance: These accounts are used to calculate PPN Terutang = PPN Keluaran - PPN Masukan when you make tax remittance payments. These settings are automatically configured and locked by the system for compliance.
descriptions.withholdingTax: Configure accounts for withholding taxes (PPh). These are optional and only used when you have withholding tax transactions.
descriptions.inventory: Configure accounts for inventory tracking and cost of goods sold. These are used when recording COGS in sales transactions.

tooltips.vat: VAT/PPN accounts are critical for tax compliance (DJP). These accounts are locked to ensure data integrity.

pph21.label: PPh 21 Account
pph21.tooltip: PPh 21 is withheld from employee salaries and services. Typically 2% for construction services, 5% for professionals. This account tracks prepaid tax that can offset your tax obligations.

pph23.label: PPh 23 Account
pph23.tooltip: PPh 23 is withheld from vendor payments for services, rent, royalties. Typically 2% for services, 15% for dividends/interest. Select the account where this prepaid tax will be recorded.

pph25.label: PPh 25 Account
pph25.tooltip: PPh 25 is corporate income tax paid monthly in installments. This is an advance payment of annual tax. Configure this if you need to track monthly tax installment payments separately.

taxPayable.label: Tax Payable Account
taxPayable.tooltip: Generic tax payable account for various tax obligations like property tax, vehicle tax, or other taxes not covered by specific accounts. This is a liability account.

inventory.label: Inventory Account
inventory.tooltip: Main inventory asset account (typically code 1301). When you sell items, the cost is deducted from this account. If you have multiple inventory types, select your main inventory account here.

cogs.label: Cost of Goods Sold Account
cogs.desc: For recording cost of sold items
cogs.tooltip: COGS expense account (typically code 5101 - Harga Pokok Penjualan). When items are sold, the cost is recorded as an expense in this account. This directly affects your profit/loss calculations.

profitLoss.title: Profit and Loss Statement
profitLoss.analysisNotAvailable: Analysis: No revenue or expense transactions found for this period. The report shows data from SSOT journal system but no income-generating or cost activities were recorded.

tooltips.grossProfit: 📈 GROSS PROFIT: Revenue minus COGS. This margin shows production/purchasing efficiency. The higher, the better!
tooltips.operatingIncome: 💼 OPERATING INCOME: Gross profit minus operating expenses. Shows profitability from core business activities before interest and taxes.
tooltips.ebitda: 📊 EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation & Amortization): Operating profit before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Shows business cash-generating ability.
tooltips.netIncome: ✨ NET INCOME: Final profit (bottom line) after all costs, taxes, interest. This shows true profitability and how much can be retained/distributed to owners.
tooltips.revenue: 💰 REVENUE: Total money received from selling goods/services to customers. This is the main source of company income before deducting costs.
tooltips.cogs: 📦 COST OF GOODS SOLD (COGS): Direct costs to produce or purchase goods sold. Includes raw materials, direct labor, and production overhead.
tooltips.operatingExpenses: 🏢 OPERATING EXPENSES: Costs to run daily business like employee salaries, office rent, electricity, marketing, administration. Does not include COGS.
tooltips.otherIncome: 🎁 OTHER INCOME: Income outside main business, such as deposit interest, asset sale gains, or rental income.
tooltips.otherExpenses: 📉 OTHER EXPENSES: Costs outside normal operations, such as loan interest, asset sale losses, or penalties.
